stem:
The GP in the practice reviews a 3-year-old boy who has coughed for 8 days. For the last 2 days the cough comes in paroxysms and he vomits afterwards. He is afebrile and active. A throat swab for pertussis PCR yesterday was negative. His 10-week-old sister lives in the same house and is well.

What should the GP do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Arrange chest X-rays and start azithromycin only if pneumonia is present
options.explanation: A chest X-ray is for an unwell infant under 6 months, when pertussis pneumonia is a concern. It should not decide treatment for this well child and his sister.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the negative throat PCR and review both children in one week
options.explanation: A negative throat swab does not exclude pertussis, and waiting a week leaves the exposed infant without prophylaxis. Send the correct specimen and act on the clinical and contact risk now.

options.label: C
options.text: Start therapeutic azithromycin for the boy only and observe the infant sister
options.explanation: The boy needs treatment, but observing the well 10-week-old misses the separate post-exposure prophylaxis recommendation for an exposed infant under 6 months.

options.label: D
options.text: Treat the boy, give the infant prophylaxis, and send a posterior nasopharyngeal PCR
options.explanation: Treat the symptomatic boy despite the insensitive throat swab; give separate post-exposure prophylaxis to the exposed infant under 6 months; send the preferred PCR specimen.

options.label: E
options.text: Repeat the throat PCR and start azithromycin only if that swab is positive
options.explanation: Repeating the less-sensitive throat specimen is the wrong test, and treatment of the symptomatic child should not wait for a positive result.

context:
A throat swab does not exclude pertussis; send a posterior nasopharyngeal PCR. Treat the symptomatic boy, while the well 10-week-old receives separate post-exposure prophylaxis as an exposed infant under 6 months.

RCH and Therapeutic Guidelines support these two actions. Their timing descriptions differ, so this item does not collapse them into one numeric cutoff.

A chest radiograph is for an unwell infant with possible pulmonary complications, not the test that decides treatment here.
